question: Can a photon-frequency anomaly make spectroscopic Galactic rotation appear faster than the transverse motion of the same sources, while leaving open a broader new optical-metric theory?

new_physics_framework.geometric_optics_limit: g_opt^mn k_m k_n=0 with g_opt^mn=g^mn+xi*S(X)*B^m B^n
new_physics_framework.regime_gate: S(X) tends to zero in high-acceleration Solar-System conditions and can approach one in galactic or cluster conditions
new_physics_framework.standard_QED_limit: ordinary curvature-QED terms remain present but are negligible; xi and the dynamical B field represent new physics
new_physics_framework.frequency_requirement: a static scalar optical index can bend rays but conserves Killing frequency; an apparent rotation signal requires a moving, vortical, direction-dependent, or explicitly time-dependent B field

observable_models.broader_optical_metric: If both channels agree, a static angular remapping cannot inflate v_transverse=4.74047*mu/parallax because the same local Jacobian multiplies mu and parallax; a surviving model must distinguish secular motion from annual parallax or be time dependent.

primary_sample.reason_for_projection_cut: Avoid dividing a nearly uninformative line-of-sight or transverse channel by a near-zero circular-motion projection.

uncertainty.fit: weighted least squares on training sources
uncertainty.validation: each complete source appears in exactly one held-out fold

frequency_only_advance_gate.context: The local outer-SPARC diagnostic needs a median 61.4 km/s apparent excess; 30 km/s is a deliberately conservative survival threshold.
requirements: cross-validated model improves held-out RMSE relative to DeltaTheta=0
full-sample 95 percent upper interval for A reaches at least 30 km/s

claim_boundary: The catalog combines heterogeneous maser transitions and uses inferred central-star motions; residual source peculiar velocities are modeled as noise.
The comparison tests a frequency-only illusion directly. Agreement of Doppler and astrometric channels does not reject explicitly time-dependent or annual-parallax-sensitive photon physics.
The Galactic constants are fixed to the Reid et al. scale; sensitivity checks must show whether the anomaly estimate is driven by this convention.
This is a Milky Way same-source test, not yet a joint fit to extragalactic spectral cubes and raw cluster lensing.
No claim of a complete quantum theory is made until the B-field dynamics, stability, causality, and radiative corrections are derived.
